html:
A teacher who led Tanganyika to independence and became the first president of Tanzania, ruling from 1961 to 1985. Tanzanians still call him Mwalimu, "teacher".

He studied at Makerere and Edinburgh, and in 1954 founded the Tanganyika African National Union. Tanganyika won independence peacefully in 1961. After the Zanzibar Revolution he joined it with Zanzibar in 1964 to form Tanzania.

  • His Arusha Declaration of 1967 set out Ujamaa, an African socialism based on village life. Moving people into planned villages, often by force, hurt farming, and the economy struggled.
  • He made Swahili the national language. Tanzania avoided the ethnic conflict of many neighbours, and literacy rose fast.
  • He backed liberation movements in southern Africa and won Chinese help to build the TAZARA Railway.
  • In 1979 his army drove Idi Amin out of Uganda.

He stepped down in 1985, admitting his economic policies had failed in part. He remained a respected voice for African unity until his death.
